name: Pregame.com
kind: Pick marketplace selling plays from many handicappers
title: Pregame.com Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Pregame.com review, checked 7 Nov 2026: real package prices from $5 picks to $1,995 a year, what its pick archive shows, the Deadspin dispute, buyer reports.
dek: A Las Vegas marketplace that sells picks from about 30 handicappers in one cart, at $5 to $30 a play or up to $1,995 for a year of one pro. It publishes a graded archive of recent pro picks, which is more than most sellers show, but the archive is kept by the company that sells the picks.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Pregame or any handicapper who sells on it. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

glance: Pregame, LLC, a Nevada LLC in Las Vegas (terms of service)
$5 a play to $1,995 for one pro for a year
None. Credit only if two bought top plays land on opposite sides
Pregame graded archive, about the last 30 days shown
short_answer: Pregame.com is a real, long running business. Its terms name the operator, Pregame, LLC of Las Vegas, it lists a toll free phone line and a support email, and it shows a price for every package. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

Pregame is a store, not one handicapper, so there is no single Pregame record. Each pro sells under his own name and advertises streaks he picks himself, such as "296-253-7 Last 556 Premium Plays" or "+374.67 UNITS". Pregame does publish a graded log of recent pro picks with odds and results, which lets a buyer check some of this, but Pregame keeps that log itself. A 2016 Deadspin analysis of Pregame's own archive found the picks sold from 2011 to May 2016 lost money overall. Pregame's founder disputed it, sued, and the case was settled.

Treat every Pregame pro as a seller with a marketing record. If you buy, buy short, compare what you get against the archive and your own log, and judge a pro after a few hundred picks, not a hot week.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on the Pregame pros page and on Dave Essler's profile, one of the most heavily promoted pros, on 7 Nov 2026. Each pro sets his own packages, so prices for other pros may differ.
pricing: Single plays and daily cards (pros page)
Dave Essler weekender, every pick through Monday night
One month football all access (several pros)
Flex Access, one pro at a time, switch up to twice a month
$195 a month, rebills unless cancelled by email
Free $25 to use on a pick
guarantee: Pregame does not offer a money back or profit guarantee on picks, and it says so on purpose. Its discount page calls "guaranteed picks" a "deceptive marketing ploy" and argues they cost more than its own picks when a handicapper wins. That argument is fair as far as it goes: a pick guarantee never covers the money you bet. The same page mentions a narrow "Money Back to Comeback" insurance offer, but we found no terms for it.

The one remedy we could read is "opposite side insurance". The FAQ links to a 2009 forum post that says if you buy two packages whose top rated plays are on opposite sides of the same game, Pregame will credit your account with what you spent on both. It applies only to the top play in each package, is paid as account credit, and you must email support to claim it. We found no cash refund terms in the FAQ or the terms of service. Flex Access rebills at $195 a month until you cancel by email.

claims_note: The streak lines are chosen by each pro and change often. Under each pro the page offers "more streaks", which means more lines the pro selected, not a full record. Some pros do post losing totals too: one showed "2026 CFB / 58-62 -19.25 Units" beside his winning lines, which is more honest than most marketing in this business.

Win and loss counts alone say little. Stephen Nover's 296-253-7 works out to about 54% winners, only a little above the roughly 52.4% needed at -110, and the line does not show the prices taken or the size of each play. Dollar figures on profiles assume a bet size per star that buyers may not match.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: very little. We found no full log of Pregame picks kept by an outside party that we could open, and no regulator record. In 2015 Pregame's founder announced that a forum member, ComptrBob, would track Steve Fezzik's Bet Like a Pro service as an "impartial third party", but that tracking lives in a thread on Pregame's own forum and we did not audit it. Fezzik cites Westgate contest results, which are run by a third party, but we did not open those results.

What Pregame itself publishes: an "Every Pro Pick Ever" page that lists pro picks with a date and time, the pro, the pick, the final score, the odds, the size, win or loss, and the dollar result. On 7 Nov 2026 its date filter covered about the last 30 days. Each profile also shows the last 10 picks and selected best records. This is more than most pick sellers show. But Pregame grades and stores it, the log does not say whether its time is the release time or the game time, and in a 2019 response the founder said picks enter the archive "soon after the game starts". A 2015 forum post says Pregame grades only at a line that at least half of representative sportsbooks offered when the pick was made.

The archive has been tested once in public. On 23 Jun 2016 Deadspin published an analysis of Pregame's archive by two bettors who scraped it, and reported that picks sold from 1 Jan 2011 through May 2016 added up to a loss of nearly $310,000 by Pregame's own grading, with 11 of 49 pros showing a profit. Deadspin's update says RJ Bell and Pregame filed a defamation lawsuit in June 2017 and the case was settled, that Deadspin links Bell's response as part of the settlement, and that Deadspin stands by its reporting. In that response Bell said Deadspin counted inactive pros, did not adjust for pros on opposite sides of the same game, and that most of Pregame's active pros were profitable. That data is now more than nine years old and says nothing certain about today's roster.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Pregame.com handicapper is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these handicappers perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Pregame's founder has written that 55% winners is the best a professional can hope for over the long run. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Pregame is thin and mostly old. Much of the talk about Pregame pros happens on Pregame's own forum, which the company hosts and moderates. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: In a thread on Pregame's own forum, a member claimed Steve Fezzik "lost -95 Units for his clients in 2025". Fezzik replied in the thread that he won just under 260 units from 2020 to 2024. Neither side posted a full log there, and we did not verify either figure.
When Pregame announced its opposite side insurance on its forum, several members praised it as customer friendly. The posts are old and sit on Pregame's own site.

ComplaintsBoard shows two complaints from 2009, both marked resolved. One buyer said the picks he bought lost while the handicappers claimed wins on the forum the next day. Another alleged that a seller promoted himself under several usernames and that critics were banned. These are unverified and more than 15 years old.

Trustpilot showed an unclaimed Pregame.com profile with 0 reviews. The Apple App Store app named PreGame is an unrelated party game from another developer. Reddit search did not load for our check, and we did not find a Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to pregame.com.

conflicts: Pregame sells the picks, grades them, keeps the archive and runs the forum where buyers discuss them. That does not make the records wrong, but no outside party checks them.

We found no sportsbook links or promo codes on the Pregame pages we opened on 7 Nov 2026, and its affiliate page says "Pregame does not have a Affiliate Program." In his 2019 response Bell wrote that Pregame does not advertise or receive revenue from any sportsbook. Deadspin's 2016 story reported that Pregame sent customers to sportsbook referral sites, and Bell denied running them. We could not confirm either side for today.
strengths: A named operator, a toll free phone line, a support email and a posted price for every package.
A public graded archive of recent pro picks with odds, size and results, plus a last 10 picks list on each profile. Most pick sellers show nothing like it.
It does not sell "guaranteed" picks, and it explains why a guarantee does not protect a bettor's stake. Free picks and a $25 join credit let you sample before paying.
concerns: The archive and every streak line come from the seller. On 7 Nov 2026 the archive filter showed only about the last 30 days.
No refund terms found. The only remedy we read is store credit when two bought top plays land on opposite sides.
Deadspin's 2016 analysis of Pregame's own data found the picks sold from 2011 to May 2016 lost money overall. Pregame disputed it, and the lawsuit was settled.
Heavy discount marketing, such as prices shown reduced from $3,000 or $5,000, and a monthly plan that rebills until you cancel by email.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business, Pregame, LLC of Las Vegas, with published prices, a support line and roughly 30 named pros. Whether those pros win over time is a separate question that we could not verify.

On 7 Nov 2026 single plays cost $5 to $30. Dave Essler's packages ran $69 for a weekend, $119 for 7 days, $249 for 30 days and $1,995 for a year, and Flex Access cost $195 a month and rebills until cancelled.
Does Pregame.com have a verified record?
Not an independent one. Pregame publishes a graded archive of recent pro picks with odds and results, but it keeps that archive itself, and no Watchdog graded record is matched to any Pregame pro.

For the money you get a pro's picks and analysis, plus a public archive you can use to check recent results, which most sellers do not offer. What is unproven is whether any pro beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of picks, and there is no refund if the picks lose.
